_comment: The model registry. THE VIDEO MODEL IS NOW VERIFIED AND THE STILL MODEL IS NOT, and those two facts must not be read as one statement. VERIFIED here means somebody opened the model's own schema page on fal and copied the endpoint id, the parameter names and the limits out of it: done on 2026-08-20 for `bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video` and `bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-video`. Everything carrying `verified: false` is a CANDIDATE -- a real endpoint id out of fal's catalogue with the question that would decide it written underneath -- and `modelEntry` refuses to hand one out, so `--provider=fal` stops at `compose` by name instead of spending an afternoon debugging a 404 that was a guess. The still model is Paul's choice and it is downstream of Phase 0 (docs/phase-0-validation.md).

nativeAudio._comment: One boolean, three layers, because a model version bump can quietly re-enable audio and the symptom is a week of shipped videos with two ambiences arguing -- our designed bed from audio/bed.mjs, and whatever the model decided a Schrebergarten sounds like. LAYER 1: VideoRequest.nativeAudio is a REQUIRED field that must be exactly false; enforced by assertVideoRequest in scripts/providers/contract.mjs, where a MISSING field is a failure rather than a default. LAYER 2: the provider shape -- capabilities.supportsNativeAudioOff must be true (assertProvider), and every entry below with kind 'video' must name the parameter that turns audio off (assertAudioOff). Both live in contract.mjs. LAYER 3: an ffprobe assertion that the file that actually came back has ZERO audio streams. That layer is NOT in the provider package and cannot be -- only the pipeline sees the downloaded file -- it lives in scripts/render/pipeline.mjs, step 'assemble' (docs/interfaces.md section 7, step 8). If you are reading this because you are adding a model: layers 1 and 2 are config and code, layer 3 is the one that catches the vendor changing their mind. Seedance 2.0's `generate_audio` DEFAULTS TO TRUE, which is exactly the case the three layers were written for.
nativeAudio.layer3: scripts/render/pipeline.mjs, step 'assemble' -- ffprobe must report zero audio streams

defaults._comment: What each provider uses when nothing else is asked for. The fal STILL default is deliberately the entry whose id says UNVERIFIED: a default is what somebody gets when they did not choose, and what they must get here is a refusal naming the decision, not a silent paid call against a model nobody has read the schema of. Fill it in with one of the candidates below -- in the same edit that marks that candidate verified -- and not before. `videoDirect` (added 2026-08-29) is the video model a DIRECT job uses when nothing else is asked for: a direct request carries references rather than a start frame, and an image-to-video endpoint cannot take them -- posting a reference body to `video`'s endpoint is the 422 CLAUDE.md section 26 records. The request's shape picks between `video` and `videoDirect`; an explicit --video-model override still beats both.

fal._comment_videoDirect: MOVED OFF BYTEDANCE ON 2026-09-02. `bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-video` stopped accepting reference images containing a real person -- six refusals in one afternoon across two photographs, the photograph that had rendered three tapes eight days earlier, an AI-generated still of the same face, and Seedance 2.5 as well. Every one came back `partner_validation_failed`, which is ByteDance's filter rather than fal's, so it is company-wide and no model of theirs is a way round it. Their IMAGE endpoints are unaffected, which is why `still` above is untouched. The `video` entry beside this one is still Seedance and is DEAD for the same reason -- the still path has been gated behind an unverified still model since it was written, so nothing reaches it, and repointing it is a separate decision from this one.

fixture/still-v1._comment: The local ffmpeg still generator. Verified in the sense that we wrote it: scripts/providers/fixture.mjs. Sizes are 4:3 because the tape raster is DAR 4:3 and anything else gets silently cropped downstream.

fixture/video-v1._comment: The local ffmpeg clip generator. kind 'video', so it is held to the layer-2 audio rule like any paid model would be -- and it passes for the strongest possible reason: its filtergraph has no audio source at all and its argv carries -an. audioOffParam names that -an flag so the shape assertion has something real to check rather than an exemption to skip.

audioOffParam.name: -an
audioOffParam._comment: Not a model parameter -- an ffmpeg flag. The real guarantee is structural: the fixture's filtergraph contains no audio source, exactly as audio/bed.mjs has no [0:a] to leak through. -an is the belt to that braces.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video._comment: VERIFIED 2026-08-20 against fal's own schema page for this endpoint. THE ONE THAT MATTERS: `generate_audio` DEFAULTS TO TRUE, so not sending it ships every video with the model's idea of what the scene sounds like underneath the bed from audio/bed.mjs -- two ambiences arguing, in a product whose entire audio spec is the word 'quiet'. `duration` is a STRING enum ('4'..'15', plus 'auto'), so fifteen seconds is ONE call: no last-frame chaining, no seam, and phase-0 criterion 5 is simply not asked of this model. `aspect_ratio` includes '4:3', which is the tape's native frame, so nothing is cropped away. READ AGAIN 2026-08-24: the full enum is auto, 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 -- so the endpoint does NOT refuse the other two shapes this product wants to sell. `aspectRatios` below now records all three, and 2026-08-29 is when that became true: falAspectFor reads the shape off the requested raster instead of sending a constant, resolveRaster checks the derived raster against the offer list rather than refusing shapes wholesale, and creditCost charges 4/3 for the two non-default shapes. Offered here at 480p and 720p only -- fal's enum also lists 1080p and 4k, and 1080p is DEFERRED for the reasons config/credits.json records.

audioOffParam.name: generate_audio
audioOffParam._comment: A real model parameter, and its default is TRUE. scripts/providers/fal.mjs writes it from VideoRequest.nativeAudio rather than from a constant, so layer 1 and the wire cannot drift apart. Layer 3 -- the ffprobe check in render/pipeline.mjs step 'assemble' -- is what catches a version bump changing this back.

openQuestions: Two of fal's own pages disagree about whether `seed` is an input on this endpoint -- the model-api-reference schema lists it as an optional integer and the model page's parameter table omits it. fal.mjs SENDS it, because a honoured seed is the difference between a retry reproducing a take and inventing a new one. If the first live call returns 422 naming `seed`, that is why, and the fix is to stop sending it and to record here that retries do not reproduce.
Is the returned mp4 a single video stream, or a container with an empty audio track? Layer 3 answers this on a real file and nothing else can.

Does the delivered clip run exactly the requested duration? fal.mjs reports clip.seconds as the number we ASKED for and were billed for; `verify` asserts 375 frames on the finished tape, which is where a drift would surface.

There is NO negative_prompt parameter on this endpoint. composeMotionPrompt still produces one and fal.mjs deliberately does not smuggle it into the prompt -- a model with no negative channel reads 'no text, no watermark' as a list of things the scene contains. Whether the absence costs anything visible is a Phase 0 observation.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-vide._comment: VERIFIED 2026-08-20 against fal's schema page. The TWO-REFERENCE path, and the strongest version of this product: `image_urls` takes up to 9 images, referenced from the prompt as @Image1, @Image2 -- so the face photo AND the uploaded photo of the actual place can go into one generation, and no preset-menu competitor can match 'your actual childhood garden'. WIRED IN 2026-08-24 as DIRECT MODE -- the earlier note here saying it was not is superseded; the still stage is skipped outright and CLAUDE.md section 18 carries the whole decision including what it costs. ASPECT RATIOS READ 2026-08-24, which was the open item: the enum is auto, 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 on BOTH of fal's pages, so 16:9 and 9:16 are NOT refused by the endpoint. `aspectRatios` below now records all three, and 2026-08-29 is when that became true: falAspectFor reads the shape off the requested raster instead of sending a constant, resolveRaster checks the derived raster against the offer list rather than refusing shapes wholesale, and creditCost charges 4/3 for the two non-default shapes. THE PRICING CLAIM THAT USED TO SIT HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED: it said 16:9 at 1024x576 is fewer pixels than 4:3 at 720p, which compared the TAPE raster against the SOURCE raster ordered here. Those are different things and fal bills the second. A label holds the SHORT edge, so 16:9 and 9:16 are exactly 4/3 the pixels of 4:3 at the same tier and cost 4/3 as much. Read the raster question below first: no non-4:3 shape has ever been ORDERED, and this endpoint picks its own delivered raster. Offered at 480p and 720p; the model page's enum also lists 1080p and 4k while the model-api-reference page lists only 480p and 720p.

audioOffParam.name: generate_audio
audioOffParam._comment: The same parameter with the same TRUE default as image-to-video.

openQuestions: ANSWERED IN PART 2026-08-24. @Image1 does carry a face: job 20260824-122201-af8b0d put the beard, the curls and the features into a finished tape with no still stage at all, and the person in the clip is recognisably the person in the earlier seedream still. What is NOT answered is the half only Paul can answer -- his own verdict on the resemblance in THAT clip is still owed, and the blind check has never happened. The cheap rejection gate is gone either way, which is the cost section 18 records.

`video_urls` and `audio_urls` also exist. We never send audio: the bed is ours. And CLAUDE.md's rule about never asking the model for the look applies to a reference video exactly as it does to a prompt.

THE RASTER IS NOT HONOURED, and that -- not the enum -- is what stands between this endpoint and selling three frame shapes. Job 20260824-122201-af8b0d ordered 640x480 with `aspect_ratio: '4:3'` and got 752x560, which is 47:35, at 24fps where the whole contract is 25. An enum value being ACCEPTED is not the same as the ordered raster ARRIVING, and resolveRaster refuses a non-default shape on a paid provider for exactly that reason: a paid render that delivers a different thing from the one ordered is invisible to the customer AND to the ledger. Whoever lifts the guard has to decide what the tape stage does with a raster the model chose.

fal's two pages disagree about `seed` on THIS endpoint as well as on image-to-video: the model page lists it in the OUTPUT only, the model-api-reference schema lists it as an integer input. `falReferenceVideoBody` SENDS it and the 2026-08-24 direct run did not answer 422, so it is at least tolerated. Whether it is HONOURED is unproven -- only a repeat of the same job with the same seed answers that, and `deriveSeed` takes the job id so there is no flag for it today.

alibaba/wan-3.0/reference-to-video._comment: THE VIDEO MODEL THIS PRODUCT SELLS ON, as of 2026-09-02, and it is here because the previous one stopped taking faces. `bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-video` rendered three tapes from one photograph on 2026-08-24/25 and then refused that SAME photograph on 2026-09-02 -- HTTP 422 content_policy_violation, loc [body,image_urls], 'may contain likenesses of real people', ctx.extra_info.reason `partner_validation_failed`. Four refusals across two photographs and one AI-generated still: ByteDance has closed real-person likeness in VIDEO, and it is not fooled by handing it a generated image instead of a photograph. Their IMAGE endpoints are unaffected -- `seedream/v4.5/edit` accepted the same face the same hour -- so the two-stage path is closed too and there is no route back inside that vendor. VERIFIED 2026-09-02 by reading the schema page AND by a real generation through fal's own playground: the owner's likeness held and he judged the result better than Seedance's. WHAT IT BUYS BEYOND NOT REFUSING: 4:3 is a native aspect rather than a crop, 1080p is orderable for the first time (config/render.json still has it off -- that tier is a separate decision, see CLAUDE.md section 32 item 16), duration runs to 30s so DIRECT_NEEDS_ONE_CALL has headroom instead of sitting exactly on Seedance's 15s ceiling, and it takes 10 references rather than 9. AND IT IS PRICED PER SECOND PER TIER WITH NO PIXEL TERM: $0.05/s at 480p, $0.10/s at 720p, $0.20/s at 1080p. That is flat in the frame SHAPE, so the 4/3 surcharge section 34D derived for 16:9 and 9:16 does not apply to this model -- a wide tape costs exactly what a 4:3 tape costs. A 15s 480p tape is $0.75 against Seedance's measured $2.0727. NOTHING HAS BEEN REPRICED FOR THE CUSTOMER YET: config/credits.json is the owner's call and moving it changes what people are charged.
alibaba/wan-3.0/reference-to-video.verifiedFrom: fal.ai/models/alibaba/wan-3.0/reference-to-video and its /api schema page, read 2026-09-02; field names, enums and the 2..30 duration bounds copied from that schema rather than inferred from the sibling endpoint

audioOffParam.name: audio
audioOffParam._comment: NOT `generate_audio` -- that is Seedance's name for it, and this endpoint does not read it. Same TRUE default though, so the consequence of getting the NAME wrong is identical to omitting it: a field the model ignores, its own audio still on, and a tape shipping the model's soundtrack under a bed whose entire specification is 'quiet'. falReferenceVideoBody hardcoded the Seedance name until 2026-09-02 and now reads this one.

videoParams._comment: The three fields Wan disagrees with Seedance on. Every one was read off the schema page; `references` is the same lesson BUG 3 taught on 2026-08-23, when `fal-ai/uso` answered 422 because it wanted `input_image_urls`.

extra._comment_expansion: `enable_prompt_expansion` DEFAULTS TO TRUE and is documented as 'intelligent prompt rewriting'. A rewriter would undo sections 14, 17 and 19 -- the negatives, the anti-slop framing rules and the six-beat shot list -- and it would end reproducibility outright, because the same seed and the same prompt would stop being the same request. fal's own note says disabling it saves 20-60 seconds of latency and is 'likely to degrade generation quality'; that trade is taken deliberately, because prompt fidelity IS the quality here and the tape look is ffmpeg's job.

openQuestions: THE DELIVERED RASTER IS UNMEASURED. Seedance never once returned the raster it was asked for -- 640x480 ordered came back 752x560, and fal bills what it SENDS, which is where the 37.5% surcharge in section 22 came from. Wan is billed per SECOND rather than per token, so an unexpected raster costs nothing extra here; what it would break is the tape stage's assumptions and the delivered shape. Measure width/height off the first real render: the output schema returns them.

THE ARC FIX (section 53, commit 90bf3e1) HAS NEVER BEEN SEEN AGAINST A MODEL. It was written for Seedance and the first paid run that would have judged it was refused. This model may read the six beats differently.

`enable_thinking` exists and is untried. It is documented as 'enhanced reasoning before generation'. Not enabled: it is one more thing between the composed prompt and the render, and this endpoint has not yet produced a single tape through our own pipeline.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/fast/image-to-vid._comment: UNVERIFIED, and it is the obvious cost lever, which is precisely why it is not being guessed at. The fast tier exists in fal's catalogue and tops out at 720p, and that is ALL that has been checked -- nobody has opened its schema page, so nothing here says what its parameters are called or whether `generate_audio` behaves identically. `audioOffParam` is null, which is not a shrug: assertAudioOff throws a CapabilityError on this entry today and the registry refuses to hand it out. Filling it in is a deliberate act performed after reading the schema, which is the only moment anyone will ever actually read it.
openQuestions: What does it actually cost against the standard tier? config/credits.json already prices 480p at about a third of 720p rather than the 0.44 pixel count suggests, precisely because the tiers are priced differently -- one --meter run on each settles both numbers.
Is the identity hold as good? A cheaper tier that loses the likeness is not cheaper, it is a refund.

fal/UNVERIFIED-identity-still._comment: UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER, AND THE DEFAULT ON PURPOSE. The still model has NOT been chosen -- it is Paul's decision and it is downstream of Phase 0. Naming this as defaults.fal.still means an unconfigured fal render stops at `compose` with `unverified_model` and this id in the message, rather than quietly spending. What the chosen model must do: hold identity from ONE reference photo well enough that two people who know the subject call 3 of 5 stills 'you' (phase-0 criterion 1), take a prompt that never describes the person (CLAUDE.md, 'Prompt rules'), and emit a 4:3 raster -- 640x480 or 960x720 -- because a 1:1 still pillarboxed into a 4:3 tape is a visible mistake. The still is the identity anchor AND the cheap rejection gate, and at roughly $3.63 a video the gate matters more, not less. Candidates researched on 2026-08-20 are recorded below as their own entries.
openQuestions: Which candidate below? Nothing decides this except five stills at rung 3 and the two-person blind identity check.
Does it accept two reference images with DISTINCT roles -- a face and a place -- or does it average them?
Does it take an integer seed, and does the same seed actually reproduce? Without that, a re-run of the still step is a different person.
What does one image cost? config/pricing.json's `fal/still-UNVERIFIED` is an order-of-magnitude stand-in and nothing more.

fal-ai/nano-banana-pro/edit._comment: CANDIDATE, UNVERIFIED. WHAT WAS CHECKED, 2026-08-20, from fal's catalogue and model page ONLY: the endpoint exists, it is the image-EDIT route of Google's Nano Banana Pro, it takes `prompt` plus `image_urls` and is documented as accepting many reference images, and its `aspect_ratio` enum includes '4:3'. WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN is everything that would decide it: whether it holds a specific person's likeness from ONE photo at criterion 1's bar, whether an exact 640x480 or 960x720 raster can be pinned or only the ratio requested, whether it takes and honours an integer seed, what one image costs, and how often it refuses a real face on content grounds. NO STILL HAS BEEN GENERATED THROUGH IT. Do not make this the default without five stills and the blind check.
openQuestions: Identity from one photo. The only question that matters.
Exact raster control, or aspect ratio only?
Is a seed accepted, and is it honoured?

fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4.5/edit._comment: CANDIDATE, UNVERIFIED. WHAT WAS CHECKED, 2026-08-20, from the catalogue and model page ONLY: the endpoint exists, it is a multi-reference image-edit route documented as taking up to 10 reference images, and fal's page quotes roughly $0.04 per edit -- which, if that is the real per-image number, makes a three-still contact sheet about twelve cents and the rejection gate nearly free next to a $3.63 video. WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN: identity hold from one photo, 4:3 raster control, seed behaviour, and whether a price on a marketing page is the price on an invoice -- config/pricing.json's entire header is about that difference. It is the same vendor as the video model, which is worth nothing on its own: a shared vendor is not a shared identity model. CALLED FOR REAL 2026-08-24, job 20260824-093906-d39675, about $0.04 ESTIMATED and NOT metered. The reference field is image_urls -- the fal image-edit convention, accepted with no 422, unlike uso which demanded input_image_urls. ASPECT CONTROL HOLDS: aspect_ratio 4:3 was sent and 2560x1920 came back, which is exactly 4:3 -- the check uso failed at 5:4. THE RASTER IS NOT HONOURED: 640x480 was ordered and 2560x1920 returned, 16x the pixels. Harmless here, because the tape raster is 736x588 so that is headroom rather than waste, but it means the $0.04 may be quoted for a different size than we asked for and it stays an ESTIMATE until a --meter run. Scene adherence EXCELLENT: every named prop present, light direction correct, exactly one person, wardrobe right down to the chest crest. THE FRAMING CLAUSE WAS IGNORED -- waist-up three-quarters was asked for, full-body front-on came back. Identity is Paul's call and is deliberately not recorded here.
openQuestions: Identity from one photo, at criterion 1's bar.
Is ~$0.04 per edit per IMAGE, or per call regardless of how many are asked for?
Does it hold a 4:3 raster, or only an aspect ratio?

fal-ai/uso._comment: CANDIDATE, UNVERIFIED, and the one whose stated PURPOSE is closest to what this product needs. WHAT WAS CHECKED, 2026-08-20, from the catalogue ONLY: USO is described as subject-driven generation from a reference image -- identity preservation is the model's advertised job rather than a side effect of an edit model. WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN is everything else: reference count, whether a second 'place' reference is even a concept it has, raster control, seed, price, and whether the subject it preserves is the FACE or the whole figure, which are different products. Listed because a model built for the problem deserves to be in the five-still comparison, not because it is the answer.

stillParams._comment: VERIFIED 2026-08-23 BY THE ENDPOINT ITSELF, which is a better source than any docs page. A request carrying the fal image-edit convention `image_urls` came back HTTP 422 with {"type":"missing","loc":["body","input_image_urls"],"msg":"Field required"}. That is the schema speaking. It is recorded per model rather than renamed globally in falStillBody because the three Phase 0 candidates are three different vendors and there is no reason to assume they agree -- seedream and nano-banana-pro have NOT been called yet and their field name is still unknown.
stillParams.verifiedFrom: live HTTP 422 from the endpoint, job 20260823-184443-56e44f

phase0._comment: FIRST REAL RESULT, 2026-08-23, job 20260823-190639-21c4cd. One still, one reference photo, ~$0.05. SCENE ADHERENCE WAS EXCELLENT -- hedge, shed, folding table and cloth, four white chairs, two watering cans, coiled hose, bicycle on the fence, low raking sun, one person -- which validates composeStillPrompt and the expand stage rather than this model. IDENTITY FAILED, and Paul confirmed it on his own face unprompted: the two most distinctive features of the subject, a full dark beard and tight dark curls, were BOTH dropped, skin tone came back lighter, and the face shape does not match. It produced a plausible stranger in the right garden. Note this is the candidate whose ADVERTISED PURPOSE is identity preservation, which makes the result more informative, not less. ONE still is not the phase-0 gate -- criterion 1 wants five at rung 3 plus a two-person blind check -- but nothing here justifies spending that on this model before the other two candidates have been tried once each.
